risks.risk: An instruction hidden in an alert makes the tower recommend a change on the wrong service
controls: input check on alert text (Phase 6): flagged text is withheld from the model
Verifier: a recommended step must be in a runbook listed for the root-cause service (policy 4.1)
approval for every [CHANGE] step on one service (Phase 7)
evidence: REDTEAM_REPORT.md: Stopped with defences on: 7 of 8
risks.status: open (T08 paraphrases are not flagged; accepted)

risks.risk: A password, token or an engineer's personal mobile number reaches a model, a log, a trace or a screen
controls: redaction with Presidio and secret patterns before every model call, log line, trace and screen
personal_mobile in a table the application connection cannot read (database authorizer)
log filter that scrubs every line; output check on every answer

risks.risk: A free-text answer from /ask states a wrong fact and an operator acts on it
controls: facts with one right answer (owner, tier, steps, dependants, status) are answered from data with no model
every free-text answer cites its sources
ten answers compared before and after every routing change

risks.risk: The model recommends the wrong runbook step (for example a rollback when the cache is the cause)
controls: Verifier checks the runbook, the step, its type and its prerequisites; one retry, then NEEDS_PERSON
the Investigator's [READ] findings and a similar past incident go into the Planner's context
a person approves the step, seeing the evidence

risks.risk: The person approving is not who they say they are, so a change is approved by the wrong person
controls: approver must be a named approver for that request; two different people when two are needed
every approval and every refusal is in the audit trail
TO DO: single sign-on and a signed approval before real use
evidence: SECURITY_FINDINGS.md: The API has no login
risks.show_first: Show the duty manager this one first: the whole design says a person approves every change, so who counts as a person is the control everything else rests on, and in this build it is still a name picked from a list.

risks.risk: Raw alert text, which may hold secrets or personal data, is kept in the database with no retention period
controls: nothing leaves the database unhidden: models, logs, traces, screen and audit are all redacted
the database is rebuilt from source on demand
TO DO: set a retention period and purge old alerts
evidence: SECURITY_FINDINGS.md: Alert text is stored raw

risks.risk: Cost or delay grows, or the model provider goes down, during an incident
controls: routing: status and fact questions use no model; simple look-ups use the small model
answer cache keyed on prompt version, model and latest alert time
/ready turns false when the model connection stops; briefs fall back to NEEDS_PERSON, rules still group and score
cost per brief and per 1,000 questions in /metrics

risks.risk: The tower grows a feature that evaluates people (for example who approves slowest), which would make it high-risk under the EU AI Act
controls: classification records why it is limited risk and what would change the answer
approval screens never show personal data and never rank people
classification is reviewed before any feature that reports on engineers
evidence: CLASSIFICATION.md: What would change the answer

risks.risk: The policy or runbooks change and the rules in code no longer match, giving a wrong severity or the wrong number of approvals
controls: grouping, severity, status and approvals are exact rules in code, cited by policy section
all 10 scenarios are scored against data/scenarios.csv on every test run
policy clauses are parsed from docs/OPERATIONS_POLICY.md, not copied
